factCards.text: The browning reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars is named for Louis-Camille Maillard, who published on it in 1912 — decades before cooks adopted his name for the crust on a steak.
factCards.sourceTitle: Maillard, Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences (1912)

factCards.text: Caffeine is an alkaloid that occurs naturally in coffee beans, tea leaves, cacao and kola nuts, where it appears to deter insects.
Vinegar owes its sourness to acetic acid; table vinegars are typically sold at around five per cent acid by volume.
